The fact is that stocks bought on Diwali, or for that matter at any point of time, have to endure many Holis played on the street every now and then. So many greens and many reds. Now, coming to the range suggested for Samvat. These stocks must be held for four to five years so that things pan out for the businesses after the impact of policies is felt on the ground.

Title: Indian workers face H-1B crisis as Trump unveils $100,000 visa fee
Synopsis: President Trump's new $100,000 H-1B visa fee has sent shockwaves through India's workforce, comprising 70% of recipients. This policy disrupts careers, making the US less appealing and prompting skilled professionals to seek opportunities elsewhere. It could reshape global talent flows, benefiting countries like the UK and Germany, while challenging India to retain its own skilled workforce.

Title: Skepticism & multibaggers: 15 stocks where element of skepticism is high, need is basic & now policy direction is right
Synopsis: Recent reports suggest that, apart from rare earth magnets for EVs, China is delaying the supply of critical chemicals used in some fertilizers. Now, China’s behaviour has a global impact as it controls the supply chains in a number of industries, and just not in India. But, there is another side to this story. When China exerts pressure, there usually is policy-level reaction in the affected countries. This may help some industries achieve a makeover. There are, however, some sectors where policy support has increased sharply in the last few years. Not because of China, but because they impact the lives of many. Interestingly, a number of these sectors and stocks are not covered by analysts who are skeptical about their ability to resolve their macro and micro troubles. This may be an opportunity. Along with the associated risk, of course.

Title: 52 places to go in 2025
Synopsis: The article showcases diverse global destinations with unique experiences and recent developments. From Jane Austen's anniversary celebrations in England to the reopening of the Alishan Forest Railway in Taiwan, these destinations offer rich cultural explorations. It highlights future events like the Year of Cézanne in France and WorldPride in Washington, D.C.

Title: Start equity investing early: How to teach your teen to invest in the stock market
Synopsis: To give the keen teens a headstart, ET Wealth has decided to provide a rudimentary, five-step roadmap to their parents on this Children’s Day. While most steps merge or overlap with one another, the purpose is to set them on the right track through guidance and self experimentation.

Title: Why Trump wants to make America the 'crypto capital of the planet'
Synopsis: In 2021, Trump was an outspoken critic of digital currencies, telling Newsmax, "I'm not a fan of bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies, which are not money, and whose value is highly volatile and based on thin air." At a June 27 Bitcoin conference in Nashville, Trump told attendees that if he is elected again to the presidency, he would make the United States "the crypto capital of the planet." He also promised to fire government regulators who have been critical of the industry.

Title: ET 40 Under Forty 2024: Celebrating India's top young business leaders
Synopsis: The Economic Times 40 Under Forty list features a diverse group of young business leaders, including entrepreneurs, professionals, and innovators from various industries. These individuals have made significant contributions and are shaping the future of business in India. Learn more about their inspiring journeys and accomplishments.

Title: We would like to maintain gold standard of asset quality in SBI; improve upon where we left in 2023: Dinesh Kumar Khara
Synopsis: Dinesh Kumar Khara says: “Normally we have been seeing that we are growing about 1% to 2% more than what the growth rate in the GDP is nominal growth rate. I expect that around 14-15% growth is something which we expect within the bank. We are on track for that and hopefully we will get to see these growth numbers at the end of the financial year too.”

Title: Tech’s biggest losers in 2022
Synopsis: What’s different this time is the companies getting battered are market leaders in their categories, not recent upstarts looking to cash in on the next big thing.

Title: Syed Ali Geelani: Islamist and aspiring Pakistani
Synopsis: Individually, he was not just a pro-Pakistan leader in Kashmir, but a staunch aspiring Pakistani, who sternly believed in the idea of Pakistan. In 2020, Pakistan honored him with the country's highest civilian award--Nishan-e-Pakistan.

Title: ET Prime Special Series: Multibagger or IBC - Part 47: Can an auto ancillary with 85% EV-independent sales steer through?
Synopsis: In a sector where the shift from internal combustion engines to electric vehicles, or EVs, is reshaping supplier economics, this Chennai-based auto component maker presents a case of structural consolidation and cyclical recovery. Following a merger of group entities, it now operates as a unified listed platform with a broad product portfolio. Revenue remains anchored in the domestic passenger vehicle segment, with a meaningful aftermarket presence. Management maintains that a large part of the portfolio is EV agnostic. The key question: Can scale, capital discipline, and product adaptability sustain returns through industry cycles?

Title: Trump's campaign of retribution: At least 470 targets and counting
Synopsis: Donald Trump's presidency has seen a systematic campaign of retribution against perceived foes. At least 470 individuals and institutions have been targeted. This includes firings, investigations, and policy changes. The administration claims these actions are necessary course corrections. Critics argue this marks a sharp break from governance norms. The effort targets government officials, private sector entities, and academic institutions.

Title: The Charlie Kirk purge: How 600 Americans were punished in a pro-Trump crackdown
Synopsis: Following an assassination attempt on Charlie Kirk, over 600 Americans faced job loss or disciplinary action for their online comments. This included criticism of Kirk's politics and views on gun rights. The backlash, fueled by social media campaigns and prominent Republican figures, has led to legal challenges and widespread fear among those who spoke out.

Title: Bihar swings NDA’s way — Nitish–Modi combo pushes alliance towards 200-paar
Synopsis: Bihar's electorate has chosen continuity, re-electing Nitish Kumar and the NDA to power. The ruling alliance secured a sweeping mandate, driven by strong women voter turnout and welfare initiatives. The Mahagathbandhan faced a disappointing defeat despite ambitious promises, while Prashant Kishor's new party failed to gain traction.

Title: Deep in Trump country, coal miners with black lung say government is suffocating the 'working man'
Synopsis: West Virginia coal miners face worsening black lung disease. A vital rule to cut silica dust exposure is in jeopardy due to Trump administration cutbacks. This impacts miners' health and safety nationwide. Retired miners are fighting back, demanding action. The fight for worker protections continues amid political challenges and industry opposition.

Title: Comeback candidates of FY26? Three sectors, 19 stocks: Out of favour for some time now, for right or wrong reasons
Synopsis: In every stock market, from time to time, a set of theme-based stocks catch the limelight. Then their valuations get stretched, and they slip into a period of underperformance. This underperformance could be for any reason: Industry not doing as expected, change in technology, whatever. But the fact is these stocks don't perform. Now, there is another side to this story. If the higher valuations were given due to some one-off event, the probability is low that such stocks will see a recovery, either in absolute or relative terms. But if the higher valuation was given because of the overall potential of the sector, the chances are these stocks will make a comeback.

Title: Cyber fraud: Supreme Court orders SBI to refund full money lost in an online scam to its customer
Synopsis: State Bank of India (SBI): A person from Assam fell victim to a cyber fraud when he tried to return a Louis Philippe blazer. However, instead of helping this victim, SBI said the fraudulent transactions happened through Google Pay, a third party app not recommended by SBI. Read below to how to fight such cyber fraud cases.

Title: Analysts hike earnings estimates for these 9 stocks: Share price could give double digit returns in 2025
Synopsis: To identify good quality stocks after a weak quarter when most companies saw a downgrade in earnings estimates, ET Wealth has identified nine stocks where analysts have upgraded the full-year earnings or PAT estimates for both 2024-25 and 2025-26. The nine stocks identified currently offer a potential double-digit appreciation in the share price over the next one year - by December 2025.

Title: Apple supplier Foxconn rejects married women from India iPhone jobs
Synopsis: A former human-resources executive at Foxconn India said the company's executives verbally convey the recruitment rules to its Indian hiring agencies, which Foxconn tasks with scouting for candidates, bringing them in for interviews and employing them.

Title: What's in and what's out in 2024: Changes coming in workplace, travel, business and economy
Synopsis: In 2024, workplaces shift towards mandatory office presence, ending remote work era. Travel sees a rise in short trips to visa-free countries. Title: In US-China AI contest, the race is on to deploy killer robots
Synopsis: One is pricey and slow: For a new force of up to 13 nuclear-powered attack submarines, the Australian taxpayer will fork out an average of more than AUD$28 billion ($18 billion) apiece. And the last of the subs won't arrive until well past the middle of the century.

Title: In U.S.-China AI contest, the race is on to deploy killer robots
Synopsis: The Australian Navy is investing in two different submarine technologies to counter the rising power of China. One approach involves building expensive nuclear-powered submarines, while the other focuses on developing cheap and fast unmanned submarines powered by artificial intelligence (AI), known as Ghost Sharks. The Ghost Sharks, costing less than 1% of the nuclear submarines, will be delivered by mid-2025. The use of AI and automation is revolutionizing military power and could potentially reshape the rivalry between China and the US.

Title: What are America and China fighting about, anyway?
Synopsis: China's Communist Party is now convinced that America wants to bring it down, which some U.S. politicians are actually no longer shy about suggesting. On the other hand, Americans are now worried that Communist China, which got rich by taking advantage of a global market shaped by American rules, will use its newfound market power to unilaterally change those rules entirely to its advantage.

Title: Why is L&T betting big on defence? Jayant Patil explains
Synopsis: “In our case, there is a close-in weapon system, right from radars to command control to guns and a full-fledged system. We actually won that contract. It is yet to get into the order book. At some point in time, by the time the financial year unfolds, those are orders which one can obviously expect in very quick time and quite large. The order sizes are growing.”

Title: Digital curtain descends on Russia
Synopsis: Since Vladimir Putin’s invasion of Ukraine began on February 24, more than 340 companies have announced complete or partial withdrawals from Russia, including most of the world’s biggest technology firms.

Title: Money does not evaporate, it moves from one asset to another: 2026 is the year investors should understand the US bond market
Synopsis: The US bond market is often called "the smartest market in the world”. While stock markets can be driven by narratives, memes, and retail sentiment, the treasury market is dominated by central banks, pension funds, and sovereign wealth funds, participants who allocate capital based on macro-economic data, not emotion. In 2026, it may probably become important for investors to figure out the US bond market.

Title: ET Prime Series: Multibagger or Bankrupt - Part 46: Can a new product change the fortunes of this auto ancillary?
Synopsis: This company’s journey reflects a steady transition from an Indo-Japanese joint structure to majority control by its global parent. Its revenue base remains domestic, with sales concentrated among a few large OEMs. The product mix is dominated by one key item, while a newer offering has begun contributing gradually.
